Estimate Person Parameters for the GPCM

Source: R/estimate.R
PP_gpcm.Rd

Compute person parameters for the GPCM and choose between five common estimation techniques: ML, WL, MAP, EAP and a robust estimation. All item parameters are treated as fixed.

Usage

PP_gpcm(
  respm,
  thres,
  slopes = NULL,
  theta_start = NULL,
  mu = NULL,
  sigma2 = NULL,
  type = "wle",
  maxsteps = 100,
  exac = 0.001,
  H = 1,
  ctrl = list(),
  range = c(-6, 6),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

respm

An integer matrix (or a data.frame), which contains the responses of the examinees. A persons x items matrix is expected. Missing responses are NA.

thres

A numeric matrix which contains the threshold parameter for each item. If the first row of the matrix is not set to zero (only zeroes in the first row) - then a row-vector with zeroes is added by default.

slopes

A numeric vector, which contains the slope parameters for each item - one parameter per item is expected. A single value is used for all items. If NULL (default), all slopes are 1.

theta_start

A vector which contains a starting value for each person. If NULL is submitted, the starting values are set automatically. If a scalar is submitted, this start value is used for each person.

mu

A numeric vector of location parameters for each person, the normal prior for MAP and EAP estimation and for PV. A single value is used for all persons. If nothing is submitted this is set to 0 for each person. MLE, WLE and robust estimation have no prior: a value given there is ignored with a warning, and the result stores NA.

sigma2

A numeric vector of variance parameters for each person, the normal prior for MAP and EAP estimation and for PV. A single value is used for all persons. If nothing is submitted this is set to 1 for each person. MLE, WLE and robust estimation have no prior: a value given there is ignored with a warning, and the result stores NA.

type

Which maximization should be applied? There are five valid entries possible: "mle", "wle", "map", "eap" and "robust". To choose between the methods, or just to get a deeper understanding the papers mentioned below are quite helpful. The default is "wle" which is a good choice in many cases. With "eap" the estimate is the mean and the SE the standard deviation of the posterior, computed on a grid of ability values (see PV). Plausible values (PV) need the prior of "eap" or "map".

maxsteps

The maximum number of Newton steps per person. Default = 100.

exac

How accurate are the estimates supposed to be? The iteration of a person stops when the step is smaller than exac. Default is 0.001.

H

In case type = "robust" a Huber ability estimate is performed, and H modulates how fast the downweighting takes place (for more Details read Schuster & Yuan 2011).

ctrl

more controls

  • killdupli: Should duplicated response pattern be removed for estimation (estimation is faster)? This is especially reasonable in case of a large number of examinees and a small number of items. Use this option with caution (for map and eap), because persons with different mu and sigma2 will have different ability estimates despite they responded identically. Default value is FALSE.

  • skipcheck: Default = FALSE. If TRUE data matrix and arguments are not checked - this saves time e.g. when you use this function for simulations.

range

The interval c(lower, upper) in which mle, wle, map and robust estimates are searched. If the estimating equation has no root inside, the estimate is set to the bound it points to and its status is "boundary". Default c(-6, 6).

verbose

If TRUE, a message names the model and the estimation type. Default FALSE.

Value

An object of class ppeo (and fourpl, gpcm or gpcm4pl), a list with

estimates

A data.frame with one row per person, in the order of respm: estimate, SE, nsteps (Newton steps of the person; 0 for eap) and status, a factor with the levels

  • "ok": converged inside range,

  • "extreme": mle or robust estimate of a person with all answers in the lowest or highest category, the estimate is -Inf or Inf and the SE NA,

  • "boundary": the estimating equation has no root inside range, the estimate is the bound,

  • "no_response": the person answered no item, estimate and SE are NA (eap: prior mean and SD),

  • "not_converged": no convergence within maxsteps.

A warning reports persons with status "boundary" or "not_converged".

type, call

The estimation type and the call.

model

The checked and prepared inputs.

resPP

The result in the layout of earlier versions: resPP$resPP is the persons x 2 matrix of estimates and SEs, resPP$nsteps the largest number of steps.

Use coef() for the estimates and as.data.frame() for the table.

Details

Please note, that robust estimation with (Huber ability estimate) polytomous items is still experimental!

The probability choosing the k-th category is as follows:

$$P(x_{ij} = k | \hat \alpha_i, \hat\beta_{iv}, \theta_j) = \frac{exp(\sum_{v=0}^{(k-1)}\hat \alpha_{i}(\theta_j - \hat \beta_{iv}))}{\,\sum_{c=0}^{m_i - 1}exp(\sum_{v=0}^{c}\hat \alpha_{i}(\theta_j - \hat \beta_{iv})))}$$

In our case \(\theta\) is to be estimated. The item parameters are assumed as fixed (usually these are estimates of a former scaling procedure).

The model simplifies to the Partial Credit Model by setting \(\alpha_{i} = 1, \forall i\).

References

Baker, Frank B., and Kim, Seock-Ho (2004). Item Response Theory - Parameter Estimation Techniques. CRC-Press.

Masters, G. N. (1982). A Rasch model for partial credit scoring. Psychometrika, 47(2), 149-174.

Muraki, Eiji (1992). A Generalized Partial Credit Model: Application of an EM Algorithm. Applied Psychological Measurement, 16, 159-176.

Muraki, Eiji (1993). Information Functions of the Generalized Partial Credit Model. Applied Psychological Measurement, 17, 351-363.

Samejima, Fumiko (1993). The bias function of the maximum likelihood estimate of ability for the dichotomous response level. Psychometrika, 58, 195-209.

Samejima, Fumiko (1993). An approximation of the bias function of the maximum likelihood estimate of a latent variable for the general case where the item responses are discrete. Psychometrika, 58, 119-138.

Schuster, C., & Yuan, K. H. (2011). Robust estimation of latent ability in item response models. Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics, 36(6), 720-735.

Wang, S. and Wang, T. (2001). Precision of Warm's Weighted Likelihood Estimates for a Polytomous Model in Computerized Adaptive Testing. Applied Psychological Measurement, 25, 317-331.

Warm, Thomas A. (1989). Weighted Likelihood Estimation Of Ability In Item Response Theory. Psychometrika, 54, 427-450.

Examples

# six items with three categories: one column of thresholds per item
thres <- matrix(c(-2, -1.23, 1.11, 3.48, 1, 2, -1, -0.2, 0.5, 1.3, -0.8, 1.5), nrow = 2)
sl <- c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 1.1, 1, 0.98)
set.seed(1750)
x <- sim_gpcm(thres = thres, alpha = sl, theta = rnorm(30))

# GPCM, weighted likelihood
resgpcm <- PP_gpcm(respm = x, thres = thres, slopes = sl, type = "wle")
summary(resgpcm)

#>

# partial credit model: all slopes 1 (the default), EAP
respcm <- PP_gpcm(respm = x, thres = thres, type = "eap")
head(respcm$estimates)

# items with a different number of categories: NA below the last threshold
thres4 <- rbind(thres, c(NA, NA, NA, NA, 1.7, 1))
x4 <- sim_gpcm(thres = thres4, alpha = sl, theta = rnorm(30))
head(PP_gpcm(respm = x4, thres = thres4, slopes = sl, type = "map")$estimates)
